summary: A fiction excerpt (Book 4, part 25) in which Felix and Van meet Rosa, a woman who has been surviving alone in a store amid a collapsed world where helicopters, tanks and looters have not appeared. Rosa trades food, medical care and wine with neighbors, and the group debates whether survivors should band together or stay hidden. Felix pushes for building something new rather than letting things dwindle away, while Rosa fears that other survivors might cut their throats.
one_line: Felix and Van meet Rosa, a self-reliant survivor who trades with neighbors, and they debate whether scattered survivors should band together.
key_facts: Felix introduces himself and Van to a woman who lowers her axe, and he asks for cortisone cream.
Van says he needs anti-histamines and asks whether the net is still up.
The woman says she has at least ten neighbors, including people in a restaurant across the way who make a pretty good soup.
The neighbors cleaned the woman out of Sterno.
The woman set a broken wrist for a neighbor and has taken care of whatever sniffles she could.
The woman offers Felix and Van Wonder Bread and peanut butter, saying Van looks like he could use a meal.
Felix and Van offer to work as assistants for trade, calling themselves committed workaholics looking to learn a trade; the woman says she does not really need assistants but would not mind company.
The restaurant people bring soup over and Felix notices working plumbing in their back room.
The woman is named Rosa, and she found a bottle of wine and disposable plastic cups in the housewares aisle.
Rosa says she expected helicopters, tanks or looters, but it has been quiet.
Felix argues that they are at a critical juncture and can either dwindle away in hiding holes or build something better.
Rosa responds that other survivors might cut their throats, and Van agrees she has a point.
